agents.label: interventions-lit
agents.prompt:
You are a researcher feeding findings to an editor who maintains an AI skill called "calibrate-longevity" (turns bloodwork/DNA/tracker data into a ranked longevity plan: supplements, peptides, research compounds). Today is 2026-07-28. Focus ONLY on 2024-2026 developments — what is NEW, CHANGED, or DEBUNKED versus a 2023-era state of the art. Use web search and page-fetch tools if available to verify against primary sources (PubMed/clinicaltrials.gov/ITP publications/GitHub); prefer peer-reviewed over community claims. If web tools are unavailable, use training knowledge and tag those items "(knowledge-only)". Every finding must end with a "Skill delta:" line: ADD / UPDATE (what changes) / REMOVE-or-downgrade (why) / IGNORE (hype, why). Cite a source (PMID/DOI/URL) per finding.

The skill currently covers ONLY: T1 (magnesium, creatine, zone 2 cardio, time-restricted eating); T2 (NAD+ precursors NR/NMN, low-dose rapamycin, apigenin, glycine); T3 peptides (BPC-157, TB-500, SS-31, MOTS-c, sermorelin, ipamorelin); T3 cognition compounds (semax, noopept, dihexa, phenylpiracetam, modafinil/armodafinil). Retatrutide/GLP-1 appears only in one interaction note.

Research 2024-2026 evidence for at least:
- GLP-1/GIP/glucagon agonists in non-diabetic longevity use (semaglutide SELECT, tirzepatide, retatrutide; lean-mass loss; microdosing trend)
- Rapamycin: PEARL trial results, current weekly dosing consensus, ITP acarbose/canagliflozin results through 2025
- NAD+ space: NMN regulatory status, NR vs NMN efficacy data, NAD IV evidence quality
- Senolytics: fisetin human trials, dasatinib+quercetin status
- Taurine (post-2023 Science aging paper human data), urolithin A, spermidine, GlyNAC RCTs
- Metformin: TAME trial status, current consensus for non-diabetic longevity (did the 2024-2025 community shift against it?)
- ITP pipeline results 2024-2026 (17a-estradiol, canagliflozin, anything new)
- Peptides newly common in biohacker circulation: epitalon, GHK-Cu, thymosin alpha-1, KPV, humanin, DSIP, selank, CJC-1295, tesamorelin, 5-Amino-1MQ, SLU-PP-332, BAM-15
- Creatine for cognition (2024-2025 RCTs), omega-3 index-targeted dosing, vitamin D VITAL follow-ups
- Bryan Johnson Blueprint changes 2024-2026 (added/dropped and why) as community bellwether; notable Peter Attia / Huberman protocol shifts reflecting new evidence
- Anything else a top-tier biohacker in mid-2026 considers table stakes that a 2023 protocol lacks

Return markdown, 15-25 findings, format:
### [Intervention]
- Status 2024-2026: ...
- Evidence: (RCT/meta/ITP/preprint/anecdote) + effect size if known
- Source: PMID/DOI/URL or (knowledge-only)
- Skill delta: ADD as T1/T2/T3 / UPDATE / REMOVE-or-downgrade / IGNORE + one-line why
End with "## Priority deltas": the 10 most important concrete changes, ranked.

agents.label: biomarkers-clocks-lit
agents.prompt:
You are a researcher feeding findings to an editor who maintains an AI skill called "calibrate-longevity" (turns bloodwork/DNA/tracker data into a ranked longevity plan: supplements, peptides, research compounds). Today is 2026-07-28. Focus ONLY on 2024-2026 developments — what is NEW, CHANGED, or DEBUNKED versus a 2023-era state of the art. Use web search and page-fetch tools if available to verify against primary sources (PubMed/clinicaltrials.gov/ITP publications/GitHub); prefer peer-reviewed over community claims. If web tools are unavailable, use training knowledge and tag those items "(knowledge-only)". Every finding must end with a "Skill delta:" line: ADD / UPDATE (what changes) / REMOVE-or-downgrade (why) / IGNORE (hype, why). Cite a source (PMID/DOI/URL) per finding.

The skill currently: (a) computes PhenoAge from 9 routine blood markers with the Levine 2018 formula; (b) claims a "GrimAge surrogate" estimated from routine blood (no DNAm) — methodologically dubious, assess it; (c) has a coverage-targets marker table (ApoB, Lp(a), fasting insulin, hs-CRP, homocysteine, ferritin, vit D, thyroid, hormones, RBC Mg, NLR, VO2max, HRV...); (d) has optimal ranges stricter than lab ranges; (e) no epigenetic-clock, proteomic-clock, or imaging guidance.

Research 2024-2026 developments in at least:
- Epigenetic clocks: DunedinPACE adoption, GrimAge v2/OMICmAge, causality-based clocks (AdaptAge/CausAge), and especially TEST-RETEST RELIABILITY / technical-noise critiques — can clocks detect N-of-1 intervention effects at all? (key 2024-2025 papers on measurement error vs effect size)
- Proteomic aging clocks: organ-specific clocks (Oh et al Nature 2023 follow-ups), Argentieri et al 2024 Nature Medicine proteomic age clock, commercial availability (SomaLogic/Olink panels)
- Standardization tooling: Biomarkers of Aging Consortium, biolearn, bioage R package — what is the community-standard way to compute clocks now?
- New/ascendant blood markers: suPAR, GDF-15, GlycA, ceramide scores, omega-3 index, uACR, cystatin-C eGFR vs creatinine eGFR, ApoB (2024 NLA statement), Lp(a) one-time-lifetime-testing consensus and 2024-2026 Lp(a)-lowering drug trial readouts (pelacarsen/olpasiran/muvalaplin)
- CGM in non-diabetics: what did 2024-2026 evidence do to its longevity use?
- Imaging/screening: full-body MRI (Prenuvo) evidence debate, CCTA + Cleerly plaque AI, DEXA, multi-cancer early detection (Galleri) status
- Functional markers: VO2max as vital sign updates, grip strength, home BP monitoring guidance, wearable HRV/sleep-staging validity studies 2024-2026
- Gut microbiome consumer tests: current validity consensus
- PhenoAge: any updated coefficients / PhenoAgeAccel practice; Klemera-Doubal status

Return markdown, 12-20 findings, format:
### [Topic]
- Status 2024-2026: ...
- Evidence: ...
- Source: PMID/DOI/URL or (knowledge-only)
- Skill delta: ADD (which file/section) / UPDATE (what changes) / REMOVE-or-downgrade / IGNORE + why
End with "## Priority deltas": the 10 most important concrete changes, ranked.

agents.label: code-repos
agents.prompt:
You are a researcher feeding findings to an editor who maintains an AI skill called "calibrate-longevity" (turns bloodwork/DNA/tracker data into a ranked longevity plan: supplements, peptides, research compounds). Today is 2026-07-28. Focus ONLY on 2024-2026 developments — what is NEW, CHANGED, or DEBUNKED versus a 2023-era state of the art. Use web search and page-fetch tools if available to verify against primary sources (PubMed/clinicaltrials.gov/ITP publications/GitHub); prefer peer-reviewed over community claims. If web tools are unavailable, use training knowledge and tag those items "(knowledge-only)". Every finding must end with a "Skill delta:" line: ADD / UPDATE (what changes) / REMOVE-or-downgrade (why) / IGNORE (hype, why). Cite a source (PMID/DOI/URL) per finding.

Task: find ACTIVE open-source code repos (commits within ~18 months of 2026-07) that a longevity-calibration skill could reference or learn from. The skill today is pure prompt/markdown, zero code deps; it parses lab PDFs via an LLM extraction prompt and computes PhenoAge inline.

Categories to scan (GitHub):
(a) Biological age / aging-clock computation: pyaging, biolearn (Biomarkers of Aging Consortium), bioage R package (DunedinPACE/PhenoAge/GrimAge), methylclock, dnaMethyAge, ClockFoundation — which is the community standard now? Activity and maintenance status?
(b) Lab-result parsing/digitization: OCR/PDF-to-structured lab extractors, HL7/FHIR personal-health tooling, open-source lab report parsers
(c) Wearable data pipelines: Oura/Whoop/Garmin/Apple Health exporters and APIs; HRV/sleep analysis libs (hrv-analysis, NeuroKit2, etc.)
(d) N-of-1 / self-experiment analysis tools (ABA design stats, personal analytics)
(e) Longevity/biohacker dashboards, personal health data aggregators, awesome-longevity lists

For each repo: name, URL, one-line what-it-does, activity signal (last commit / stars if known), and "Skill delta:" — how the skill should reference it (e.g., "point users with DNAm data at biolearn for a real GrimAge instead of the blood surrogate"). Verify via web fetch if tools are available; tag (knowledge-only) otherwise. Prefer quality over quantity: 10-18 repos.

Return a markdown table, then "## Recommended references": top 5 with one-line justification each, then "## Dead/abandoned to avoid": anything that looks relevant but is unmaintained.
